conflicts_resolved_manually.description:
True only when `manual_resolution_state` was captured by an actual
human conflict resolution (`heddle sync` materialized conflicts, then
`heddle resolve` cleared them). False when the same field was set by a
fully-automatic conflict-free integration (e.g. a clean 3-way merge of
two threads that touch disjoint files). Both populate
`manual_resolution_state` to mark the thread land-ready, but only the
former should be reported as "manually resolved" to the operator.
Pre-existing on-disk records have no field and serde defaults to
`false`, so a stale clean-merge record never claims a manual resolution.

ThreadMode.description:
How a thread's worktree is realised on disk. Three flavours:

* [`ThreadMode::Materialized`] — clonefile-or-reflink the captured
  tree into a thread directory. Real `read(2)`-able bytes, ~zero
  disk cost via shared extents (APFS / btrfs / XFS w/ reflinks).
  Day-one default on reflink-capable filesystems and the path the
  stat-cache fast no-op + manifest sidecar were built for. See
  `docs/design/clonefile-threads.md`.
* [`ThreadMode::Virtualized`] — project the captured tree through
  a content-addressed FUSE/FSKit/ProjFS mount. Nothing on disk
  until the kernel asks. Useful for repos too large to materialize
  or when the CAS is remote-backed.
* [`ThreadMode::Solid`] — full file copies with no shared extents.
  Strong isolation; the only choice on ext4 / NTFS hosts that have
  neither reflinks nor a usable mount API.

The discriminant names match the user-facing `--workspace` flag
values so a single vocabulary spans the CLI, the JSON contract,
and the thread record on disk. Pre-rename data using the older
`"lightweight"` (clonefile) / `"materialized"` (full-copy) names
will fail to deserialize and require a re-export — intentional;
silently degrading isolation modes is the wrong default.

ThreadMode.description:

  tree into a thread directory. Real `read(2)`-able bytes, ~zero
  disk cost via shared extents (APFS / btrfs / XFS w/ reflinks).

  stat-cache fast no-op + manifest sidecar were built for. See
  `docs/design/clonefile-threads.md`.

  a content-addressed FUSE/FSKit/ProjFS mount. Nothing on disk
  until the kernel asks. Useful for repos too large to materialize
  or when the CAS is remote-backed.

  Strong isolation; the only choice on ext4 / NTFS hosts that have
  neither reflinks nor a usable mount API.

`"lightweight"` (clonefile) / `"materialized"` (full-copy) names

recovery_state.description:
heddle#305: the pre-undo state preserved for recovery, and the marker
pointing at it. Present only on a completed `undo`; omitted from the
wire when absent (preview / redo).

agent_may_fill.description:
Whether an agent may replace placeholders in `argv_template`.

When `agent_may_fill` is false, treat `action` and `argv_template` as
display-only: do not substitute `<name>`/`<url>` placeholders. Surface
the template to a human or discard it. Substituting and running it will
pass literal `<name>` to Heddle and fail.

id.description: Numeric oplog id, useful for downstream cursor tracking.

roles.description:
Resource roles the caller holds directly (UI gating only; the server
enforces effective, inherited roles on each RPC).

server_scope.description: The scope string the server records for this credential.

authenticated.description: A usable credential resolves for this server.

capture_actor.description: Who the next capture is attributed to. Distinct from hosted auth.

expires_at.description: Effective token expiry (RFC3339). `None` ⇒ no expiry recorded.

operation_ceiling.description:
The intersected hosted-operation ceiling from the delegation chain.
`None` ⇒ no operation allowlist (full authority).

proof_key_available.description: The device proof key needed to sign hosted requests is present and valid.

reachable.description: The server answered `WhoAmI` — the hosted identity below is authoritative.

scopes.description:
Resource scopes the delegation chain restricts this token to. Empty ⇒
full resource authority.

subject.description: Locally verified subject, present even when the server is unreachable.

token_kind.description:
`root` (full-authority device/human token), `agent` (an offline-derived,
attenuated delegation), or `service-account`. `None` when unauthenticated.

ttl_seconds_remaining.description: Seconds until `expires_at`; negative when already expired.
